questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The quantities which have the same dimensions as those of solid angle are:
questions.explanation: Solid angle is dimensionless. Strain and angle are also dimensionless quantities.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a vernier calipers, (N + 1) divisions of vernier scale coincide with N divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is:
questions.explanation: (N+1) VSD = N MSD, so 1 VSD = N/(N+1) MSD. Least Count = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = MSD x [1 - N/(N+1)] = MSD/(N+1) = 0.1mm/(N+1) = [1/(10N... )]; converting units: LC = 1/(100(N+1)) cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A horizontal force 10 N is applied to a block A as shown in figure: block A (2 kg) and block B (3 kg) rest side by side in contact on a frictionless horizontal surface; the force F=10N is applied horizontally to the left face of block A, pushing both blocks to the right. The mass of blocks A and B are 2 kg and 3 kg, respectively. The blocks slide over a frictionless surface. The force exerted by block A on block B is:
questions.explanation: Common acceleration a = F_net/M_total = 10/5 = 2 m/s^2. Force exerted by A on B = mass_B x a = 3 x 2 = 6 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle moving with uniform speed in a circular path maintains
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion the speed (magnitude of velocity) is constant, but the direction of velocity changes continuously, so velocity varies. Since the direction of centripetal acceleration also keeps changing, acceleration varies too.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A bob is whirled in a horizontal plane by means of a string with an initial speed of w rpm. The tension in the string is T. If speed becomes 2w while keeping the same radius, the tension in the string becomes:
questions.explanation: T = M w^2 r, so T is proportional to w^2. Doubling w quadruples T, so the new tension is 4T.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: At any instant of time t, the displacement of any particle is given by 2t - 1 (SI unit) under the influence of force of 5 N. The value of instantaneous power is (in SI unit):
questions.explanation: s = 2t - 1, so v = ds/dt = 2 (SI unit). Instantaneous power P = F.v = 5 x 2 = 10 (SI unit).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity v1 while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is v2. The ratio v1 : v2 is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum: m v1 + 0 = 2m v2, so v1 = 2 v2, giving v1 : v2 = 2 : 1.

questions.topic: Moment of Inertia, Theorem of Parallel and Perpendicular Axis and Energy in Rotation

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question_text: A wheel of a bullock cart is rolling on a level road as shown in the figure below: a spoked circular wheel with point P marked at the very top and point Q marked at the very bottom (point of contact with the ground), rolling to the right with linear speed v (arrow shown at the wheel's centre height, pointing right). If its linear speed is v in the direction shown, which one of the following options is correct (P and Q are any highest and lowest points on the wheel, respectively)?

options.a: Both the points P and Q move with equal speed.
options.c: Point P moves slower than point Q.
options.d: Point P moves faster than point Q.

questions.explanation: For a rolling wheel, the point of contact with the surface (lowest point, Q) has zero velocity, while the highest point (P) moves with twice the velocity of the centre of mass. So point P moves faster than point Q.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Newton's Law of Gravitation & Acceleration Due to Gravity
questions.question_text: The mass of a planet is 1/10th that of the earth and its diameter is half that of the earth. The acceleration due to gravity on that planet is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The maximum elongation of a steel wire of 1 m length if the elastic limit of steel and its Young's modulus, respectively, are 8 x 10^8 N/m^2 and 2 x 10^11 N/m^2, is:
questions.explanation: Young's modulus = stress_max/strain_max, so strain_max = 8x10^8 / 2x10^11 = 4x10^-3. Elongation = strain x length = 4x10^-3 x 1m = 4 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A thin flat circular disc of radius 4.5 cm is placed gently over the surface of water. If surface tension of water is 0.07 N/m, then the excess force required to take it away from the surface is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Thermodynamic Processes and First Law of Thermodynamics
questions.question_text: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cycle abcda, shown on a P-V diagram: point a at (V=100cm3, P=100kPa), point b at (V=400cm3, P=100kPa), point c at (V=400cm3, P=300kPa), point d at (V=100cm3, P=300kPa) - forming a rectangle traversed a->b->c->d->a. The work done by the gas along the path bc is:
questions.explanation: Since volume is constant along path bc (an isochoric segment), the work done W = integral of P dV = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If x = 5 sin(pi*t + pi/3) m represents the motion on a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the amplitude and time period of motion, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: Comparing x = 5 sin(pi*t + pi/3) with standard SHM x = A sin(w t + phi): Amplitude A = 5 m. Angular frequency w = pi rad/s, so time period T = 2*pi/w = 2*pi/pi = 2 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The potential (V) at any axial point, at 2 m distance (r) from the centre of the dipole of dipole moment vector P of magnitude 4 x 10^-6 C m, is +/- 9 x 10^3 V. (Take 1/(4 pi epsilon0) = 9x10^9 SI units)
Reason R: V = +/- 2KP/r^2, where r is the distance of any axial point, situated at 2 m from the centre of the dipole.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: A is true but R is false.
options.b: A is false but R is true.
options.c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.d: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.explanation: V = KP cos(theta)/r^2; for an axial point theta=0 or 180, so V = +/- KP/r^2 = +/- 9x10^9 x 4x10^-6 / 2^2 = +/- 9x10^3 V. Assertion A is correct (numeric value matches). However Reason R as stated uses an incorrect factor, so R is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A thin spherical shell is charged by some source (charge q = 1 microcoulomb, radius R = 3 cm), shown with point C at the centre and point P on/at the shell's surface. The potential difference between the two points C and P (in V) shown in the given figure is: (Take 1/(4 pi epsilon0) = 9x10^9 SI units)
questions.explanation: For a charged spherical shell, the potential at the centre equals the potential at the surface (V_centre = V_surface, since the field inside is zero and hence potential is uniform inside). The potential difference between C (centre) and P (surface) is therefore zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In the following circuit, five 2 microfarad capacitors are arranged as a bridge network between terminal A and terminal B: the top path has two 2uF capacitors in series (A to a middle node to B), the bottom path has two 2uF capacitors in series (A to another middle node to B), and a fifth 2uF capacitor bridges the two middle nodes vertically. The equivalent capacitance between terminal A and terminal B is:
questions.explanation: This is a symmetric (balanced) bridge network, so no charge flows through the bridging (middle) 2uF capacitor and it can be ignored. The top branch (two 2uF in series) gives 1uF; the bottom branch (two 2uF in series) gives 1uF; these two 1uF branches are in parallel between A and B, giving 1+1 = 2uF.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A wire of length 'l' and resistance 100 Ohm is divided into 10 equal parts. The first 5 parts are connected in series while the next 5 parts are connected in parallel. The two combinations are again connected in series. The resistance of this final combination is:
questions.explanation: Each of the 10 parts has resistance 10 Ohm. First 5 in series = 50 Ohm. Next 5 in parallel = 10/5 = 2 Ohm. Total (series combination of the two groups) = 50 + 2 = 52 Ohm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Internal Resistance of a Cell and Grouping
questions.question_text: The terminal voltage of the battery, whose emf is 10V and internal resistance 1 Ohm, when connected through an external resistance of 4 Ohm as shown in the figure is: (circuit: a single loop with a 4 Ohm resistor on the top branch and, on the bottom branch, a 10V EMF source in series with a 1 Ohm internal resistance)
questions.explanation: Current i = EMF/(R+r) = 10/(4+1) = 2A. Terminal voltage = EMF - i*r = 10 - 1(2) = 8 V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A tightly wound 100 turns coil of radius 10 cm carries a current of 7 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is (Take permeability of free space as 4*pi x 10^-7 SI units):

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Material): A. Diamagnetic, B. Ferromagnetic, C. Paramagnetic, D. Non-magnetic
List-II (Susceptibility chi): I. chi = 0, II. 0 > chi >= -1, III. chi >> 1, IV. 0 < chi < epsilon (a small positive number)
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic materials: small negative susceptibility (-10^-5 to -10^-9), matching II (0 > chi >= -1). Ferromagnetic: chi >> 1, matching III. Paramagnetic: small positive susceptibility, matching IV. Non-magnetic: chi = 0, matching I. So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A strong bar magnet (N pole on the left, S pole on the right) is moving with velocity v to the right, positioned between Solenoid-1 (on its left, with terminals A at bottom and B at top) and Solenoid-2 (on its right, with terminals C at bottom and D at top) - i.e. the magnet is moving away from solenoid-1 and towards solenoid-2. In the above diagram, the direction of induced current in solenoid-1 and that in solenoid-2, respectively, are through the directions:
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law, as the magnet moves away from solenoid-1 and towards solenoid-2, the induced currents oppose the change in flux in each solenoid respectively, giving current directions AB in solenoid-1 and DC in solenoid-2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In a uniform magnetic field of 0.049 T, a magnetic needle performs 20 complete oscillations in 5 seconds as shown: the needle (drawn as a narrow rhombus/lozenge, with its N end labeled and S end labeled) is suspended by a thread from a fixed ceiling support, oscillating in a horizontal magnetic field B (shown as horizontal dashed arrows pointing right). The moment of inertia of the needle is 9.8 x 10^-6 kg m2. If the magnitude of magnetic moment of the needle is x x 10^-5 Am2; then the value of 'x' is:

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: In an ideal transformer, the turns ratio is Np/Ns = 1/2. The ratio Vs : Vp is equal to (the symbols carry their usual meaning):
questions.explanation: Transformation ratio r = Ns/Np = Vs/Vp. Given Np/Ns = 1/2, so Ns/Np = 2, meaning Vs/Vp = 2, i.e. Vs : Vp = 2 : 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction Through Prism and Dispersion Through Prism
questions.question_text: A light ray enters through a right angled prism (triangle ABC, right angle implied at B, with vertex A at top, B at bottom-left, C at bottom-right) at point P on face AB with the angle of incidence 30 degrees as shown in figure. It travels through the prism parallel to its base BC and emerges along the face AC. The refractive index of the prism is:

options.d: 5/2 (per source; the mathematically-derived answer is sqrt(5)/2, see explanation)

questions.explanation: At surface AB: 1*sin30 = mu*sin(r). Since the ray travels parallel to base BC inside a right-angled prism and emerges along face AC at the critical/grazing condition: mu*sin(90-r)=1, i.e. mu*cos(r)=1, so cos(r)=1/mu. From sin30=mu*sin(r)=0.5, sin(r)=1/(2mu), and sin^2(r)+cos^2(r)=1 gives 1/(4mu^2) + 1/mu^2 = 1... solving yields mu^2 = 5/4, so mu = sqrt(5)/2. This is the value the answer key labels as option (d).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Interference and Young's Double Slit Experiment
questions.question_text: If the monochromatic source in Young's double slit experiment is replaced by white light, then

options.a: there will be a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
options.b: all bright fringes will be of equal width.
options.d: there will be a central dark fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.

questions.explanation: With white light, the central fringe (zero path difference, same for all wavelengths) appears white; fringes of other colours form at different positions on either side, giving a central white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Polarization Phenomenon, Law of Malus and Brewster's Law
questions.question_text: An unpolarised light beam strikes a glass surface at Brewster's angle. Then

options.a: both the reflected and refracted light will be completely polarised.
options.b: the reflected light will be completely polarised but the refracted light will be partially polarised.
options.c: the reflected light will be partially polarised.
options.d: the refracted light will be completely polarised.

questions.explanation: At Brewster's angle, only the reflected light is completely polarised; the refracted light remains partially polarised.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question_text: The graph which shows the variation of 1/lambda^2 and its kinetic energy, E is (where lambda is de Broglie wavelength of a free particle): four small graphs of 1/lambda^2 (y-axis) vs E (x-axis) - (a) a curve that rises steeply then flattens (concave down, like sqrt(E)); (b) a straight line through the origin with constant positive slope; (c) a curve that starts flat and rises steeply (concave up, like E^2); (d) a decreasing curve (falling from high to low as E increases).

options.a: Concave-down curve through the origin (rises steeply then flattens as E increases).
options.b: Straight line through the origin with constant slope.
options.c: Concave-up curve through the origin (rises slowly then steeply as E increases).
options.d: Decreasing curve (1/lambda^2 falls as E increases).

questions.explanation: lambda = h/p = h/sqrt(2mE), so 1/lambda^2 = 2mE/h^2, i.e. 1/lambda^2 is directly proportional to E - a straight line through the origin with constant positive slope. Option (b) matches this.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Parameters of Photon (Momentum, Pressure and Energy)
questions.question_text:
If c is the velocity of light in free space, the correct statements about photon among the following are:
A. The energy of a photon is E = hv
B. The velocity of a photon is c.
C. The momentum of a photon, p = hv/c
D. In a photon-electron collision, both total energy and total momentum are conserved.
E. Photon possesses positive charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.b: A, B, D and E only
options.d: A, B, C and D only

questions.explanation: A photon has energy E=hv (A, true), travels at velocity c (B, true), has momentum p=hv/c=h/lambda (C, true), and in photon-electron collisions both total energy and momentum are conserved (D, true, since no external force acts). Photons are chargeless (E, false). So A, B, C and D only.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Alpha-Particle Scattering and Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Atoms are electrically neutral as they contain equal number of positive and negative charges.
Statement II: Atoms of each element are stable and emit their characteristic spectrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.b: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: atoms are electrically neutral, having equal numbers of positive and negative charges. Statement II is incorrect: it is atoms of most elements (not literally 'each' element, and emission occurs when excited, not simply because they are 'stable') that emit characteristic spectra; per the answer key, Statement II is judged incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Bohr H-atom Model, Radius of Orbit, Velocity and Energy of Electrons, Wavelengths of Hydrogen Spectrum and Ionisation
questions.question_text:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Spectral Lines of Hydrogen for transitions from): A. n2=3 to n1=2, B. n2=4 to n1=2, C. n2=5 to n1=2, D. n2=6 to n1=2
List II (Wavelengths (nm)): I. 410.2, II. 434.1, III. 656.3, IV. 486.1
questions.explanation: Using 1/lambda = RZ^2(1/n1^2 - 1/n2^2) for hydrogen (Z=1), the Balmer series wavelengths are: n2=3->n1=2: 656.3nm (III); n2=4->n1=2: 486.1nm (IV); n2=5->n1=2: 434.1nm (II); n2=6->n1=2: 410.2nm (I). So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: 290/82 X --alpha--> Y --e+--> Z --beta(minus)--> P --e(minus)--> Q. In the nuclear emission stated above, the mass number and atomic number of the product Q respectively, are:
questions.explanation: X(290,82) --alpha(-4 mass,-2 atomic)--> Y(286,80) --e+ positron emission(atomic -1)--> Z(286,79) --beta-minus(atomic +1)--> P(286,80) --e- emission, i.e. another beta-minus-type electron emission (atomic +1)--> Q(286,81). Alpha emission decreases mass number by 4 and atomic number by 2. Both the e+ and beta-minus/e- steps change only the atomic number (positron emission decreases it by 1, electron/beta-minus emission increases it by 1); mass number is unchanged by either. Final product Q has mass number 286 and atomic number 81, option (b).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statement A and B and identify the correct answer, referring to a standard four-quadrant I-V axis diagram (quadrants I, II, III, IV labeled around the origin, V on the horizontal axis, I on the vertical axis):
A. For a solar-cell, the I-V characteristics lies in the IV quadrant of the given graph.
B. In a reverse biased pn junction diode, the current measured in (A), is due to majority charge carriers.

options.a: Both A and B are correct.
options.b: Both A and B are incorrect.
options.c: A is correct but B is incorrect.
options.d: A is incorrect but B is correct.

questions.explanation: A solar cell's I-V characteristic indeed lies in the fourth quadrant (it supplies power rather than drawing it) - A is correct. In reverse bias, the small current that flows is due to minority charge carriers, not majority - B is incorrect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
A logic circuit provides the output Y as per the following truth table:
A=0,B=0 -> Y=1
A=0,B=1 -> Y=0
A=1,B=0 -> Y=1
A=1,B=1 -> Y=0
The expression for the output Y is:
questions.explanation: Testing Y = B-bar (NOT B) against the truth table: B=0 -> Y=1 (matches both A=0,B=0 and A=1,B=0 rows); B=1 -> Y=0 (matches both A=0,B=1 and A=1,B=1 rows). Y depends only on B and equals NOT B in every row, matching option (a).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The output (Y) of the given logic gate is similar to the output of an/a: the circuit takes inputs A and B, each first passed through a NOR-shaped gate (bubble output) combined into a further NOR-shaped gate producing output Y - equivalent overall to an AND gate.
questions.explanation: The given combination of NOR-type gates (bubbled OR gates) reduces algebraically to output Y = A.B (a NOT-OR-of-NOTs construction, which is a standard way to build an AND gate from NOR gates), matching an AND gate, option (b).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A force defined by F = at^2 + bt acts on a particle at given time t. The factor which is dimensionless, if a and b are constants, is:
questions.explanation: [MLT-2] = a[T2] so a=[MLT-4]. [MLT-2] = b[T] so b=[MLT-3]. at/b = [MLT-4][T]/[MLT-3] = [M0L0T0], dimensionless.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The velocity (v) - time (t) plot of the motion of a body is a trapezoid: v rises linearly from 0 (segment A to B, positive constant slope), stays constant (flat top, segment B to C, zero slope), then decreases linearly back toward 0 (segment C to D, negative constant slope). The acceleration (a) - time (t) graph that best suits this motion is: four small a-t graphs (a) a graph with a positive constant-value rectangle segment then a negative constant-value rectangle segment (step function, matching the two constant-slope portions of the v-t graph, with zero in between); (b) a graph with a negative rectangle segment then a rising ramp; (c) a graph with a smooth flat-topped trapezoid/hump shape; (d) a graph with a ramp rising to a plateau.

options.a: Step function: positive constant value (matching A-B), then zero (matching B-C), then negative constant value (matching C-D).
options.b: A negative constant-value rectangle followed by a rising diagonal line.
options.d: A rising ramp that levels off into a plateau.

questions.explanation: From A to B, the v-t slope is positive and constant, so acceleration is a positive constant value. From B to C, slope is zero, so acceleration is zero. From C to D, slope is negative and constant, so acceleration is a negative constant value. This step-function pattern (positive constant, then zero, then negative constant) matches option (a).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Satellite, Orbital Velocity and Escape Velocity
questions.question_text: The minimum energy required to launch a satellite of mass m from the surface of earth of mass M and radius R in a circular orbit at an altitude of 2R from the surface of the earth is:
questions.explanation: Initial total energy (on surface) = -GMm/R. Final total energy (orbit at altitude 2R, so orbital radius 3R) = PE + KE = -GMm/(3R) + (1/2)(GM/(3R))m = -GMm/(6R). Minimum energy required = E_final - E_initial = -GMm/(6R) - (-GMm/R) = 5GMm/(6R).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A metallic bar of Young's modulus 0.5 x 10^11 N/m2 and coefficient of linear thermal expansion 10^-5 /degC, length 1m and area of cross-section 10^-3 m2 is heated from 0 degC to 100 degC without expansion or bending. The compressive force developed in it is:
questions.explanation: Thermal stress = thermal strain x Y, so F/A = (alpha x delta_T) x Y. F = (10^-5 x 100 x 0.5x10^11) x 10^-3 = 50 x 10^3 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Ideal Gas Equations and Vander Waals Relation
questions.question_text: The following graph represents the T-V curves of an ideal gas (where T is the temperature and V the volume) at three pressures P1, P2 and P3, shown as three curved isobar lines compared against Charles's-law dotted reference lines; the curves are ordered from left/steepest (P1) to right/shallowest (P3), with P2 in between.
questions.explanation: By Charles's law, V is proportional to T at constant pressure, and at a given T, higher pressure corresponds to a lower-slope (steeper on T-axis) line, i.e. the order shown in the given graph is P1 > P2 > P3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: If the mass of the bob in a simple pendulum is increased to thrice its original mass and its length is made half its original length, then the new time period of oscillation is x/sqrt(2) times its original time period. Then the value of x is:
questions.explanation: T = 2*pi*sqrt(l/g) is independent of mass. New length l'=l/2, so T' = 2*pi*sqrt(l/(2g)) = T/sqrt(2). Given T' = (x/sqrt(2))*T, we get x/sqrt(2) = 1/sqrt(2), so x = 1... per the printed worked solution, x = sqrt(2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
If the plates of a parallel plate capacitor connected to a battery are moved close to each other, then
A. the charge stored in it increases.
B. the energy stored in it decreases.
C. its capacitance increases.
D. the ratio of charge to its potential remains the same.
E. the product of charge and voltage increases.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the given below:
questions.explanation: With the battery still connected, V remains constant. C = epsilon0*A/d increases as d decreases (C correct). Since Q=CV and V is constant, Q increases as C increases (A correct). Energy E=(1/2)CV^2 increases as C increases, so B (decreases) is incorrect. The ratio Q/V = C changes (increases), so D is incorrect. Product QV = CV^2 increases (E correct). So A, C and E only.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Choose the correct circuit which can achieve the bridge balance: four Wheatstone-bridge circuit diagrams (options a-d), each showing the same four resistor values arranged in a diamond - 10 Ohm (top-left arm), 10 Ohm (top-right arm), 15 Ohm (bottom-left arm), 5 Ohm (bottom-right arm) - with a galvanometer G in one diagonal and a diode D (drawn as a circled diode symbol) in the other diagonal/bridging position, a battery E and key K in the main loop; the four options differ in the orientation/placement of the diode D relative to the bridge.

options.a: uncertain - circuit diagram not recoverable from text extraction
options.b: uncertain - circuit diagram not recoverable from text extraction
options.c: uncertain - circuit diagram not recoverable from text extraction (identified in explanation as correct, with the diode/bridge arm treated as non-ideal 10 Ohm resistance)
options.d: uncertain - circuit diagram not recoverable from text extraction

questions.explanation: In option (c), if the diode is considered non-ideal with a resistance of 10 Ohm, the bridge can be balanced (i.e. the ratio of resistances in the two arms matches, giving zero galvanometer deflection).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: Two heaters A and B have power rating of 1 kW and 2 kW, respectively. Those two are first connected in series and then in parallel to a fixed power source. The ratio of power outputs for these two cases is:
questions.explanation: P_parallel = P1+P2 = 1+2 = 3kW. 1/P_series = 1/P1 + 1/P2 = 1 + 1/2 = 3/2, so P_series = 2/3 kW. Ratio P_series : P_parallel = (2/3) : 3 = 2 : 9.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An iron bar of length L has magnetic moment M. It is bent at the middle of its length such that the two arms make an angle 60 degrees with each other. The magnetic moment of this new magnet is:
questions.explanation: M = m x L (pole strength m times length L). Pole strength m stays the same after bending. When bent at 60 degrees at the midpoint, the effective distance between the two poles (L_eff) becomes L/2. New magnetic moment M_new = m x L_eff = m x (L/2) = M/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic Dipole Moment, and Force Between Magnetic Poles
questions.question_text:
A sheet is placed on a horizontal surface in front of a strong magnetic pole. A force is needed to:
A. hold the sheet there if it is magnetic.
B. hold the sheet there if it is non-magnetic.
C. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is conducting.
D. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is both, non-conducting and non-polar.
Choose the correct statement(s) from the options given below:
questions.explanation: If the sheet is magnetic, the pole exerts an attractive force on it, so a force is needed to hold it in place (A correct). If it is conducting, moving it away induces eddy currents that oppose the motion, requiring a force to move it at uniform velocity (C correct). A non-magnetic sheet requires no holding force (B incorrect). A non-conducting, non-polar sheet has no induced magnetization and needs no force to move (D incorrect). So A and C only.

questions.topic: Properties and Applications of Electromagnetic Waves
questions.question_text: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that:

options.a: they travel with speed equal to 1/sqrt(mu0*epsilon0).
options.b: they originate from charges moving with uniform speed.
options.d: the energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field.

questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating (not uniformly moving) charges. So option (b) is NOT a true property of EM waves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting it to a battery through a resistor. If I is the current in the circuit, then in the gap between the plates:

options.a: displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in a direction opposite to that of I.
options.b: displacement current of magnitude greater than I flows but can be in any direction.
options.d: displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in the same direction as I.

questions.explanation: Displacement current Id = epsilon0 * d(Phi_E)/dt, which works out to Id = dQ/dt = conduction current I, flowing in the same direction as the conduction current I in the circuit, maintaining current continuity through the capacitor gap.

questions.question_text: A small telescope has an objective of focal length 140 cm and an eye piece of focal length 5.0 cm. The magnifying power of telescope for viewing a distant object is:
questions.explanation: For normal adjustment, magnifying power M = -f0/fe = -140/5 = -28 (magnitude 28).
